name: In-game anti-cheat & player-behaviour features
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: In-game anti-cheat and player-behaviour features for competitive multiplayer titles (per-player headshot rate, per-player APM, per-player win-streak velocity, per-lobby kick-rate, per-IP/per-account aimbot-signal aggregation, smurf detection from per-(account, MMR) tenure features, MMR-boosting and matchmaking-manipulation detection, account-sharing detection on (account, IP/device) tenure, voice/chat-toxicity rate per player, vote-kick abuse per kicker and per kickee)
domain_fit.one_line_definition: A game-platform integrity / matchmaking service decides on every gameplay tick, match-end, lobby-join or vote-kick event — typically within tens to hundreds of milliseconds — whether to flag, shadow-ban, queue for manual review, downrank, MMR-correct or hard-ban a player, based on rolling per-player / per-account / per-IP / per-lobby velocity, distribution, accuracy and tenure features.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: 1) Detect aimbot / triggerbot / wallhack signal in near-real-time by maintaining rolling per-player aim features (headshot %, time-to-target, mouse-delta entropy, ADS-to-fire latency distribution, distance-to-target distribution on hits, kill-snap angular-velocity distribution) and firing a model or threshold the moment the distribution diverges from the player's historical baseline. HAWK and AntiCheatPT-style papers, plus Riot's published Vanguard pipeline, all consume essentially this feature shape. 2) Smurf and rank-boost detection by tracking per-(account, current_MMR) tenure features (games_played_at_bucket, accuracy_at_bucket, KDA, win-streak velocity, APM_zscore_vs_bucket) — Riot's Automated Smurf Detection rolled out globally in 2024 reduces smurf accounts by ~17 % and places smurfs into correct MMR 2–3x faster, and the underlying signal is rolling per-account performance vs current bucket. 3) Detect MMR-boosting / account-sharing by maintaining per-account rolling features against (account_id, ip_hash, device_fp) pairs and flagging 10–15 game win-streaks that 'shock' the matchmaker, plus impossible-travel-style distance signals on consecutive logins. 4) Detect vote-kick / lobby-griefing abuse by per-kicker (count(initiate_kick, 24h), n_unique(target, 24h)) and per-kickee (count(kicked, 7d)) features — CS2 already imposes cooldowns based on this exact aggregate shape. 5) Feed downstream ML scorers (gradient-boosted aimbot classifier, transformer time-series cheat classifier, Graph Neural Network coordinated-boosting detector) with consistent rolling features on the per-tick path (in-match throttle / kick) and the post-match path (ban-wave queue). 6) Feed matchmaking with continuously-updated player skill / trust features so that new accounts with aimbot signals never reach ranked queues in the first place.
domain_fit.event_shapes: Typical events landing in beava as @bv.event: player_input_tick {ts, match_id, player_id, mouse_dx, mouse_dy, view_yaw, view_pitch, key_state_bits, frame_time_ms} (sampled or aggregated client-side), shot_fired {ts, match_id, player_id, weapon_id, view_yaw, view_pitch, ads_state, target_player_id?, hit_bool, headshot_bool, distance_m, kill_bool}, kill_event {ts, match_id, killer_id, victim_id, weapon_id, headshot_bool, wallbang_bool, snap_angular_velocity_deg_s, time_since_visible_ms}, match_end {ts, match_id, player_id, kda, score, win_bool, mmr_before, mmr_after, hs_pct, accuracy_pct, apm}, lobby_event {ts, lobby_id, player_id, event_type (join|leave|kick|vote_kick_initiate|vote_kick_target|vote_kick_yes|vote_kick_no)}, login_event {ts, account_id, ip_hash, device_fp, hwid_hash, region, vpn_flag, residential_proxy_flag}, report_player {ts, reporter_id, target_id, reason_code, match_id}, voice_chat_segment {ts, lobby_id, speaker_id, toxicity_score, duration_ms}, anticheat_signal {ts, account_id, signal_type (driver_blocked|integrity_fail|hook_detected|byte_pattern_hit|hardware_id_change), severity}. The high-rate streams are player_input_tick (typically pre-aggregated to per-second windows client-side at the BattlEye / EAC / Vanguard agent) and shot_fired; match_end is comparatively low-rate but feature-dense.
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Heavy use of beava counter / velocity / distance / distribution / n_unique primitives over sliding windows (last 10 matches, last 1h, last 24h, last 7d, last season). Per-player: count(shot_fired), count(hit), accuracy = hit / fired (rolling), count(headshot) / count(kill) (rolling HS %), distribution(time_to_target_ms) and distribution(snap_angular_velocity_deg_s) (the two canonical aimbot tells — both shift toward low-variance, bimodal distributions under aimbot), velocity(apm), velocity(headshots), velocity(kill), distance(view_yaw_t, view_yaw_t-1) over micro-windows for flick-detection, n_unique(weapon_id, 24h) (low diversity flags scripted plays). Per-(account, MMR_bucket): count(games), distribution(kda), distribution(hs_pct), velocity(win_streak), z-score(accuracy_vs_bucket_mean) — the canonical smurf signal. Per-IP and per-hwid: n_unique(account_id, 7d) (account-farming / smurf farm fanout), count(account_create, 24h), distribution(account_age_at_first_match_min). Per-(reporter, target): count(report, 7d) (retaliatory reporting). Per-lobby / per-match: count(vote_kick_initiate, lobby), n_unique(kick_target, by_kicker_24h), count(kicked, by_kickee_7d). Per-account anti-cheat-signal aggregation: count(integrity_fail, 24h), n_unique(signal_type, 24h). Distance primitive cleanly expresses impossible-travel (login_ip_t vs login_ip_t-1) used in account-sharing / boost-takeover detection.
domain_fit.entity_grain: Composite and high-cardinality. Primary keys: account_id / player_id, match_id, lobby_id, ip_hash, hwid_hash / device_fp, and ordered pairs / triples (account_id, MMR_bucket), (account_id, ip_hash), (account_id, weapon_id), (kicker_id, kickee_id), (reporter_id, target_id). Match-time per-tick features are keyed on (match_id, player_id); long-term reputation features are keyed on account_id alone.
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: All three families show up. Tumbling per-match (a match is a natural session — most aim metrics reset and re-baseline per match). Sliding for rolling-trust features (last 10 matches, last 24 h, last 7 d). Session windows align cleanly with match boundaries. Approximate aggregates (HLL for n_unique accounts per IP, CMS for top-K offending players per region, T-Digest for headshot-rate and snap-angle-velocity distributions, Bloom for known-cheat-account membership) are acceptable everywhere — anti-cheat decisions are monotonic in the signal and 1–3 % HLL error is invisible against the manual-review threshold. Ban-wave decisions are typically aggregated and committed off Parquet event logs (not live counters) so they tolerate the approximate path.
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: At-least-once with idempotent counters keyed on event_id is sufficient. Cheat detection is not money — a duplicate-counted shot biases accuracy mildly toward the cheating side, which is safe (more likely to flag). Strict no-double-count is required only for matchmaking MMR updates (which run on a separate, transactionally-safe path) and for the formal ban-record audit log (which is in a relational store, not in beava).

technical_fit.latency_budget: Three operating points. (a) In-match tick path (kill-cam, vote-kick gating, instant-throttle): p99 < 50 ms feature-fetch is the workable budget; modern competitive shooters run 64–128 tick servers (Valorant 128, CS2 64, Fortnite 30), so anything within a tick is invisible to the player. (b) Match-end / lobby-transition path: p99 < 500 ms is typical for the 'should this account be queued for review before the next ranked match' decision. (c) Asynchronous ban-wave / analyst-queue path: seconds-to-tens-of-seconds is fine. Beava's published sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get fits all three with headroom; the per-decision feature fan-out is moderate (20–60 features on the per-match path, 60–150 on the model-scoring path).
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Sub-second for the in-match anti-cheat path (an aimbot can pop heads for an entire match before stale features catch up — Riot specifically architected Vanguard with an edge feature store caching mouse deltas and frame-time jitter for exactly this reason). Single-digit seconds for the match-end / smurf path (Riot's smurf detector targets correct MMR within 4 matches, ≈ 60–80 min for typical Valorant cadence). Sub-minute for the report-queue path. Beava's push-on-event model with no broker hop is materially fresher than the Kafka -> Flink -> Redis pipeline most in-house stacks ship today. [uncertain]
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Highly title-dependent. Fortnite's published number is ~125M events/minute ≈ 2.08M EPS sustained globally into Kinesis. A single competitive-shooter match (10 players, 64–128 tick) generates 640–1280 input-tick events/sec per match server before aggregation, plus 10–60 shot-fired and 1–4 kill events/sec — call it ~1500 EPS per match. A regional match-server fleet (1k–10k concurrent matches) is therefore 1.5M–15M EPS; a global title at Valorant / CS2 / PUBG scale is 10M–100M EPS aggregated. Per-region or per-shard, sustained 50k–500k EPS is typical, with bursts during major patches and esports events. Beava's published ~684k EPS (M4, TCP+msgpack, parallel=16) on a single core covers one regional shard with headroom, but a global AAA title needs horizontal partitioning that beava v0 does not yet ship. Mid-size studio with one regional cluster (Indie battle-royale, mid-tier MOBA, mid-tier extraction shooter) typically sees 5k–100k EPS and fits on one beava node. [uncertain]
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Roughly 2:1 to 5:1 reads-per-write on the in-match path (each shot_fired / kill_event triggers one write and one batch_get of 20–60 features to score the action), and 10:1+ on the match-end / matchmaking / smurf-bucket path where the same per-account features are re-fetched for every queue decision. Overall balanced-to-read-leaning, less extreme than recsys.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: Dominated by account_id and match_id cardinality. A mid-sized competitive title (~10M MAU, ~30M matches/month, ~3M weekly active) holds ~10M live accounts × ~80–150 counter slots × ~32 B per slot ≈ 25–50 GB hot account state, plus per-match state (rolling ~1M live matches × ~10 players × ~30 slots × 32 B ≈ 10 GB), plus IP / device-fingerprint state (typically 10–100M live IPs × ~10 slots ≈ 5–30 GB) — total 50–150 GB live state on a single box, comfortably in RAM. Fortnite / Valorant / PUBG / CoD at global scale (100M+ MAU) overflows a single beava node and requires horizontal partitioning. [uncertain]
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Slowly-growing on account_id (MAU plus signup rate, smurfs add ~10–30 % churn), explosive on match_id (millions of new matches per day on AAA titles — TTL is mandatory), explosive on (account, weapon, map) triples (Cartesian, must cap), bounded on weapon_id / map_id / lobby_type (CMS / direct count appropriate). IP_hash is explosive due to mobile IP churn and VPNs / residential proxies; HLL n_unique(account, by_ip, 7d) is the right primitive.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Mixed. In-match features: lifetime of the match (15–60 minutes). Rolling reputation / aim-baseline features: 7–30 days sliding. Smurf-detection per-(account, MMR_bucket) tenure: 30–90 days (entire competitive season). Long-term cheat-history per-account: years (ban records and chronic-offender flags). Per-IP / per-fingerprint counters: 7–30 days. Per-match state must be evictable on match-end + grace window because match_id cardinality is unbounded.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 20–60 features per in-match decision (player aim distribution + player movement entropy + per-weapon accuracy + per-match KDA + IP / device reputation + recent anti-cheat-signal counts). 60–150 features on the model-scoring path (HAWK and AntiCheatPT-style transformers consume hundreds of windowed features). Strongly favours the batch_get path beava ships.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Best-effort to crash-safe. In-match aim features are derived state — a node losing its 15-minute window during a crash produces a few minutes of degraded recall, not a regulatory or financial breach. Ban-wave decisions and matchmaking-MMR updates run off persistent stores (relational DB + warehouse), not off live counters. Beava's WAL + snapshot story comfortably covers the integrity-feature durability needs. Note: appealable ban evidence must be archived in an auditable warehouse (regulator + DSA / GDPR pressure on appeal trails), not pulled from in-memory counters that can age out.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Strong fit for single-binary regional / sidecar deployments alongside the match-server fleet or the matchmaking service. Competitive shooter architectures are already regional (Riot deploys per-region matchmaking and per-region anti-cheat verdict services); beava's single-binary model maps directly. Multi-region active-active is desired by the largest publishers (Tencent, Riot, Activision, Epic) but not strictly required for a regional shard. Hard ceilings: beava v0 has no in-process sharding (a single tenant beyond ~684k EPS or ~100 GB hot state must hand-shard externally — which is required at AAA global scale), no native multi-tenancy (vendors like Anybrain / GGWP serving many studios on one box have no isolation primitives), no triggers (anti-cheat fundamentally wants 'fire when accuracy_z > 4 over last 200 shots'), refuse-on-network-FS forces local-disk WAL planning.

commercial_fit.who_buys: (a) Game-integrity / anti-cheat engineering teams inside AAA publishers (Riot's Anti-Cheat / Vanguard team, Activision's RICOCHET team, Epic's EAC / Fortnite Trust & Safety, Bungie's BattleEye team, EA's anti-cheat ops, Take-Two / Rockstar's R* Online safety org, Roblox's Sentinel / Byfron-Hyperion team, Tencent's ACE org, NetEase Yidun, Krafton's PUBG Studios anti-cheat team, Bohemia Interactive / BattlEye, Sony PlayStation Trust & Safety). (b) Matchmaking and competitive-integrity teams (the same publishers' ranked-mode and esports-integrity orgs — Riot Esports Integrity, ESIC for tournament-level ban-list sync). (c) Anti-cheat and behavioural-fraud vendors who would embed beava rather than buy a competitor's managed feature store — GGWP (raised $12M seed led by Bitkraft + $10M follow-on + reported $15M Series A; backed by Riot Games among others), Anybrain (Portuguese AI behavioural anti-cheat), Modulate (ToxMod voice moderation), Getgud.io, FACEIT Anti-Cheat, ESEA, Vac-net-style tools, Hive AI for image moderation in user-generated levels, Sumsub for KYC on platform signup. (d) Esports operators (FACEIT, ESL, ESEA, BLAST, Riot Esports) running tournament-grade detection on top of the publisher anti-cheat. (e) Console-platform safety teams (Sony PSN, Microsoft Xbox / Community Sift, Nintendo). Buyer persona: Anti-Cheat Eng / Game Integrity / Trust & Safety Platform Eng — distinct from corporate Risk and from Growth.
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Sized in two ways. (1) Anti-cheat software / services market: analyst estimates cluster around USD 0.5–13.5B in 2024–2025 depending on scope, with CAGRs of ~9–15 % through 2032–2034 (Verified Market Research ~USD 13.5B 2024 -> USD 23.86B 2032 at 8.67 %; Growth Market Reports ~USD 538M 2024 -> USD 1.57B 2033 at 14.8 %; Dataintelo / Market Research Intellect ~USD 2.8B 2025 -> USD 7.6B 2034 at 11.7 %). Wide spread reflects whether voice / chat moderation, behavioural analytics, and infrastructure spend are bundled in. (2) Underlying game-industry spend: global online gaming market ~USD 280–340B in 2025, with publishers spending an estimated 1–3 % of revenue on integrity / anti-cheat depending on competitive-mode exposure (Riot, Activision, Epic publicly cite multi-hundred-person anti-cheat orgs; Anybrain / GGWP enterprise contracts run six- to seven-figure annually). Vendor scale: Anti-Cheat Expert (Tencent ACE) publicly cites >99.99 % accuracy and serves Honor of Kings / PUBG Mobile / Delta Force / Arena Breakout — a single deployment shape larger than most behavioural fraud markets. Modulate's ToxMod processes 'millions of hours' of voice per month and works with 'billions of voice' minutes processed by core. Roblox Hyperion (Byfron) protects ~80M+ DAU. Riot bans ~60k Valorant accounts per week as of early 2025 (≈ 3M / year), implying the candidate-event volume passing through the detection pipeline is orders of magnitude higher. [uncertain]
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: 1) AI-driven cheats (computer-vision aimbots, DMA hardware cheats, LLM-driven scripting) are pushing AAA publishers from kernel-only detection to behavioural / server-side detection — Riot's xda-developers interview and Data + AI Summit 2025 talk both explicitly cite this shift; Activision's RICOCHET ML aimbot detection was a Data + AI Summit 2025 session. 2) Regulatory pressure: EU GDPR / DMA review of kernel-level anti-cheat (2025 lobbying, 2K Borderlands EULA controversy, Helldivers 2 GDPR complaints), EU DSA transparency obligations on platforms over 45M MAU (which captures Valorant, Fortnite, CoD, Roblox), UK OSA child-safety duties (effective 25 July 2025, force Roblox / Epic / Microsoft to invest), Australia Online Safety Act, KOSA in the US, China Notice on Anti-Addiction. 3) Competitive integrity / esports pressure — ESIC bans, Valve VAC-net upgrades, FACEIT / ESL escalating ban lists; the cheat economy is now estimated in low billions USD/year. 4) Player-retention economics — Riot publicly states Valorant ranked games with cheaters are now <1 %, and that this directly impacts retention; the cost of one ranked match ruined by a cheater is estimated at multiple hours of subsequent churn. 5) Existing tooling pain: in-house teams running Redis + Lua + Flink for velocity features publicly cite ops overhead at Discord-scale, and the same pattern repeats at game-studio scale.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: GDPR (Reg 2016/679) for European players — anti-cheat data collection must satisfy data minimization, purpose limitation, and informed consent; 2025 cases (2K Borderlands EULA, Helldivers 2 kernel controversy, Vanguard petition) show active enforcement risk and force publishers to limit and document feature retention. EU DSA (Reg 2022/2065) — game platforms over 45M MAU classified as VLOPs may have transparency-report obligations on banning / appeals; Implementing Regulation 2025/1714 quantitative templates apply from 1 July 2025. EU AI Act — automated banning decisions may qualify as 'high-risk AI' if they substantially affect access to a service; documentation / explainability obligations from 2026. UK Online Safety Act 2023 — illegal-harms duties effective 17 March 2025 and children's-safety duties effective 25 July 2025; Ofcom enforcement powers including fines up to 10 % of global revenue. KOSA (US) and parallel state laws (CA AADC, NY SAFE for Kids, UT Social Media Regulation). China Notice on the Prevention of Online Gaming Addiction (real-name + facial verification for minors). PCI / SOC 2 are table stakes for any AAA publisher procurement. CSAM regimes (US 18 USC 2258A NCMEC reporting) — orthogonal but relevant on UGC-game platforms (Roblox). Right-to-erasure (GDPR Art. 17) requires cascading deletion through derived aggregates — non-trivial for in-memory feature stores; argues for short TTL + aggressive hashing of IP / hwid.
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: Fast — 1–3 days to a working per-player headshot-rate + per-player APM + per-(kicker, kickee) vote-kick demo on beava using simulated CS2-style events. A realistic 30–60-feature production pilot at a mid-sized studio is a 3–8 week effort once auth and TLS are added (the v0 gaps below). A 'smurf + win-streak + impossible-travel' triple-demo using the @bv.event / @bv.table / distance primitive is the obvious one-page README example for this vertical.

competition.incumbents: Generic real-time stack: Redis (counters + Lua, plus Redis Stack with Bloom / CMS / Top-K modules) is the default for per-player rolling features at most studios. Aerospike for highest-cardinality state (Sony PlayStation, EA). Kafka + Flink / Materialize / RisingWave at studios with a streaming backbone (Riot, Epic, Activision all run Kafka + Flink + Spark pipelines on Databricks — confirmed at Data + AI Summit 2025). Tecton / Hopsworks / Chalk / Fennel as managed online feature stores feeding XGBoost / transformer cheat classifiers. Custom in-Rust services on top of RocksDB / Sled at Roblox-scale and Riot-scale. ClickHouse for the analyst / OLAP path. Databricks for the offline ML training path (Riot, Activision, EA all publicly use it).
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Kernel / client-side anti-cheat agents (out of scope for beava, complementary): Riot Vanguard (boot-start driver, allowlist-based, Valorant + League of Legends), Easy Anti-Cheat (Epic-owned, Fortnite + many third-party titles), BattlEye (independent, ARMA / DayZ / R6 / PUBG / Destiny 2), RICOCHET (Activision, Call of Duty), Tencent ACE (PUBG Mobile, Honor of Kings, Delta Force, Arena Breakout Infinite), NetEase AntiCheat Experts / Yidun, Roblox Hyperion (Byfron, acquired by Roblox), Valve VAC + VAC-net, FairFight (legacy, EA). Server-side / behavioural-AI anti-cheat vendors (closest competition to beava as a substrate): Anybrain (AI behavioural, 99 % accuracy claim, mouse-dynamics + 70+ parameters), GGWP (AI community moderation + anti-cheat-adjacent player-trust scoring, backed by Riot Games / Bitkraft / Makers Fund / Sony Innovation Fund / Samsung / SK Telecom), Modulate ToxMod (voice toxicity), Getgud.io (real-time anti-cheat analytics for FPS), FACEIT Anti-Cheat (esports-grade), ESEA Client. Behavioural-toxicity / community-moderation overlap: Hive AI, Spectrum Labs / ActiveFence-Alice, Two Hat / Microsoft Community Sift (Xbox + Roblox). Beava would naturally sit underneath one of these vendors or inside a publisher's in-house Anti-Cheat-Eng org, not replace the kernel agent or the ML model itself.
competition.beava_differentiator: 1) Single binary, no Kafka / Flink / Redis cluster — fits the per-region / per-shard / per-match-server sidecar topology that AAA matchmaking architectures actually use (Riot deploys regional verdict services; Epic runs per-region matchmaking on AWS Kinesis; Tencent runs per-region ACE clusters). 2) 50+ aggregation primitives natively cover the velocity / accuracy / distribution / distance features anti-cheat literally lives on — including beava's distance primitive which directly expresses both impossible-travel for boost-takeover detection and view-angle-snap distance for aimbot detection, without writing Flink SQL or Redis Lua. 3) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get fits the in-match per-tick latency budget; many publishers today gate behavioural checks to match-end because the tick-path is too tight, which beava could close and Riot's 'edge feature store caching mouse deltas and frame-time jitter' confirms is the target shape. 4) Apache-2.0, no open-core — attractive to mid-tier studios (Bungie, Bohemia, Hi-Rez, Embark, Wildcard, Larian, Krafton, NCSoft, Pearl Abyss, mid-tier MOBAs and battle-royales) that cannot or will not procure Riot Vanguard / Tencent ACE / RICOCHET, and attractive to anti-cheat vendors (Anybrain, Getgud, FACEIT) who want to embed a substrate without depending on a competitor's managed cloud. 5) Push-on-event ingestion (HTTP/JSON, framed TCP, msgpack) maps directly to how match servers and anti-cheat agents already shape events (BattlEye / EAC / Vanguard already speak encrypted-binary protocols to their backends — TCP+msgpack is a natural fit). 6) Native composite-key aggregations — (kicker_id, kickee_id), (account_id, MMR_bucket), (account_id, ip_hash), (account_id, weapon_id) are first-class in @bv.table; Redis requires hand-rolled hash-of-hash schemes. 7) Refuse-on-network-FS bias actually maps well to a match-server sidecar pattern where local-NVMe WAL is the natural durability story.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: 1) No TLS / no auth on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 — disqualifying for any production deployment by a regulated publisher; effectively limits beava to in-VPC / behind-mTLS-proxy deployments. AAA studios under SOC 2 / GDPR / DSA exposure require authenticated access to integrity infrastructure. 2) No in-process sharding — Riot / Activision / Epic / Tencent / Roblox global-scale match-servers run at 10M–100M EPS aggregated, blowing past a single beava node; beava v0 forces external hand-sharding which AAA in-house teams already do but vendors (Anybrain, GGWP) cannot easily ship. 3) No triggers / 'fire when accuracy_z > 4 over last 200 shots' — anti-cheat is fundamentally event-driven (quarantine the match, shadow-ban, drop to spectator, queue for review), and polling 30 features per kill event just to threshold them wastes round-trips on the hot path. This is the single most-cited workflow gap for this domain. 4) In-memory only — anti-cheat ban evidence is appealable (GDPR Art. 22, EU AI Act if classified high-risk) and must be archived to an auditable warehouse; beava is not that warehouse and the integration pattern needs to be documented. 5) No multi-tenancy primitives — vendor like Anybrain / GGWP / Getgud serving many studios needs per-tenant namespaces, quotas and per-tenant rate-limit accounting that beava doesn't ship. 6) No secondary indexes / no 'list top-K accounts by accuracy_z in last 1 h' query — kills the analyst surface. 7) No native graph / pair-clustering primitives for coordinated boosting / win-trading detection (which CIB-style time-correlation graphs catch, hard in pure KV velocity features). 8) No native PII-handling: hwid / IP-hashing at rest, configurable retention windows, right-to-erasure cascading through aggregates (GDPR Art. 17 + DSA + EU AI Act, plus active 2025 enforcement risk on kernel anti-cheat). 9) No published benchmark on tick-rate sustained EPS with 30–60-feature batch_get; the 684k EPS number is push-only and the read-path concurrency story under that load needs to be measured for this domain. 10) No integration with the kernel-anti-cheat backend protocols (Vanguard, EAC, BattlEye, ACE all have proprietary binary wire formats and beava is not a drop-in for those — it sits above them as a feature backend).
competition.integration_surface: Producers: match server itself (Unreal Engine / Unity / proprietary engines — HTTP/JSON or TCP push from a server-side anti-cheat plugin), kernel anti-cheat backend (Vanguard vgauth.exe / EAC service / BattlEye BEService / ACE cloud — these emit verdicts and integrity events that beava would consume as anticheat_signal events), matchmaking service (per-account MMR + game-result writes), Kafka / Kinesis for publishers with a streaming backbone (Fortnite uses Kinesis at ~125M events/min; Riot uses Kafka into Databricks). Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 fits the application-server and webhook producer; TCP+msgpack :8081 fits high-throughput match-server gateways. Consumers: rules engines (publisher-internal cooldown / vote-kick logic, similar to CS2's automatic cooldown for repeat kick-initiators), ML scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM aimbot classifiers, transformer time-series cheat detectors as in HAWK / AntiCheatPT, Graph Neural Network coordinated-boost detectors as in Riot's Data+AI Summit 2025 pipeline), and inline allow / shadow-ban / friction logic at the matchmaking RPC boundary. Crucially beava does NOT replace the kernel anti-cheat agent or the ML model — it is the feature backend underneath both.
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Publishers run deterministic rules (CS2-style 'kick initiator >N in 24h => 24h cooldown', Valorant 'integrity_fail >M => instant ban', Riot 'win-streak >15 from new account => MMR recalibration shock') alongside ML scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM aimbot classifiers, transformer time-series cheat models like AntiCheatPT, GBM ensembles + GNNs as described in Riot's 2025 pipeline). Beava as a pure feature backend stays decoupled from both — same batch_get path feeds rule evaluation and ML scoring, which is its natural seam.

adoption_signals.existing_public_users_or_case_studies: No public users of beava on this use case yet. Activision — 'Machine Learning Aimbot Detection in Call of Duty' at Data + AI Summit 2025, RICOCHET kernel + server-side combined ('multi-faceted approach'). Roblox — open-sourced Sentinel August 2025 for grooming detection (256-tick context windows, 35 % of CSAM-related cases caught pre-report Jan-Jun 2025, ~6B chat msgs/day); Hyperion (Byfron, acquired by Roblox) is the kernel anti-cheat layer underneath. Tencent ACE — public partnerships with Cathedral / Asphere announced GDC 2025; 99.99 % accuracy claim; serves Honor of Kings / PUBG Mobile / Delta Force / Arena Breakout. adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: Maximum. Anti-cheat is one of the most adversarial domains in software — cheats retool weekly (DMA hardware cheats, computer-vision aimbots that read frames only, AI-driven scripting, account-marketplace smurf farms, residential-proxy / SIM-farm IP rotation, kernel-level rootkit cheats). Cheat-economy is estimated at low-billions USD/year. Feature drift is fast; integrity teams add and retire features continuously (Riot's xda interview, Vanguard patch-notes cadence). This strongly argues for a developer-ergonomic feature backend (beava's @bv.event / @bv.table model) rather than SQL-on-Flink pipelines that need schema migrations. Comparable in drift-rate to financial fraud, possibly higher in iteration cadence (weekly cheat updates vs monthly fraud-pattern updates).

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: 1) Kernel-mode integrity / driver-level cheat detection — that's Vanguard / EAC / BattlEye / RICOCHET / ACE territory and requires Ring 0 drivers, signed-driver allowlists, TPM attestation; beava is server-side feature aggregation only. 2) ML model serving / inference — XGBoost / LightGBM / transformer cheat classifiers run on KServe / Triton / Vertex / SageMaker / Databricks Serving, not in beava. 3) Long historical lookback for ban-appeal evidence (GDPR Art. 22, EU AI Act high-risk obligations require explainable decisions over months of data) — beava is in-memory; that belongs in Parquet / a lakehouse. 4) Cross-entity graph clustering for coordinated win-trading / boosting rings — beava has no join engine; graph DB / OLAP problem. 5) Full event archive / forensic match replay — WAL is for crash recovery, not analyst replay. 6) Acting as the rules engine, the matchmaking algorithm, the appeals UI, or the ban-record system of record — beava is the feature backend only. 7) Voice / chat content classification (Modulate / Hive / Perspective / Roblox Sentinel territory) — beava can count toxicity-events per player but cannot classify raw audio / text. 8) Multi-region active-active in v0. 9) Strict regulator-grade durability for ban-record audit — beava could do crash-safe live features but the ban record itself must be in a relational + warehouse store. 10) DMA / hardware-cheat detection (requires hardware-level signals beava cannot ingest).
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: Concrete features beava would need to ship to be production-grade for in-game anti-cheat, roughly in priority order: 1) TLS termination and mutual TLS on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 plus an auth model (token, mTLS, or both) on the push and admin surfaces — without this, no AAA publisher (GDPR / DSA / SOC 2 exposure) or anti-cheat-as-a-service vendor (Anybrain, GGWP, Getgud) can deploy externally; this is the same blocker as bot-defence and T&S. 2) Triggers / 'fire callback when (account_id).accuracy_z > 4 over last 200 shots' — anti-cheat is fundamentally event-driven and polling 30 features per shot event wastes round-trips on the hot tick path; documented as the single most-cited workflow gap for this domain alongside auth. 3) HLL / Bloom / CMS / Top-K approximate primitives as first-class — needed to keep account_id × ip_hash × hwid_hash cardinality in bounded RAM during ban-wave hunts; if these are already in the 50+ primitives, document them prominently for this domain with a 'top-K accounts by accuracy_z over last 1 h' worked example. 4) In-process or sidecar sharding by key prefix (account_id, match_id, ip_hash) so global-scale titles beyond ~684k EPS scale within one cluster without external hand-sharding. 5) Per-key TTL / sliding-window eviction so explosive match_id cardinality (millions/day at AAA scale) doesn't OOM. 6) Multi-tenancy: per-tenant namespaces, quotas, per-tenant rate-limit accounting for anti-cheat vendors serving many studios. 7) Streaming admin / debug surface and secondary indexes so anti-cheat analysts run 'top-K accounts by velocity(headshots) in last 1 h' or 'top-K (kicker, kickee) pairs in last 24 h' without materializing the keyspace. 8) Native PII-handling story: IP / hwid / device-fp hashing at rest, configurable per-namespace retention, right-to-erasure cascading (GDPR Art. 17 + EU AI Act explainability + DSA). 9) Composite-key (pair / triple) aggregations as first-class: (account, MMR_bucket), (kicker, kickee), (account, ip_hash), (account, weapon_id) — these are the natural anti-cheat grains and need to be ergonomic in the @bv.table DSL. 10) Documented hooks for kernel-anti-cheat-verdict enrichment (external Vanguard / EAC / BattlEye / ACE / RICOCHET service pushes verdict and integrity-fail counts into beava as anticheat_signal events). 11) Cold-start strategy: WAL replay time on a node with tens of GB of hot account / match state must be benchmarked; a node restart during esports finals would be an outage. 12) Published per-tick benchmark with 30–60-feature batch_get under read load to confirm the in-match latency budget. 13) Reference architecture for the warehouse-side appeals / DSA / EU-AI-Act audit trail (Parquet / Iceberg sink for ban evidence). 14) Documented integration pattern with Discord Social SDK / Photon Voice / Unity / Unreal anti-cheat plugins. 15) Worked example of the distance primitive for both view-angle-snap detection and impossible-travel boost-takeover, to make the differentiator concrete.
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes — strongly. Anti-cheat genuinely needs an event-driven trigger primitive: 'when (account_id).accuracy_z over 200-shot window crosses 4, shadow-ban for review'; 'when (kicker_id).kick_initiate_24h crosses 5, impose cooldown' (CS2 already does exactly this); 'when (account_id, MMR_bucket).win_streak crosses 10 and account_age < 7d, trigger smurf-calibration shock' (Riot already does this); 'when account_id.integrity_fail_24h crosses 1, instant hard-ban' (Vanguard / RICOCHET pattern). Polling 30+ features on every tick / shot just to threshold them is workable on the in-match path because the read is already happening, but is wasteful on the asynchronous match-end / ban-wave / SOC-alert path. This is one of the two most-cited gaps for the domain along with TLS + auth.
